description:
Record money received against threads, and produce billed-vs-received statements.

Subcommands:
  log THREAD AMOUNT [-c CCY] [-d DATE] [-t HH:MM] [-a ACCOUNT] [-n NOTE ...] — record a receipt
  list [THREAD] [--since D] [--until D] [--json] — list payments
  statement [--thread T] [--since D] [--until D] [--as-of D] [--pdf PATH] [--opening D] [--json] — billed vs received, by thread and currency
  show ID [--json] — show one payment
  edit ID [--amount AMOUNT] [-c CCY] [-d DATE] [-t HH:MM] [-a ACCOUNT] [-n NOTE ...] — change fields of a payment
  rm ID -y — permanently delete a payment

Args:
  THREAD, T: a thread name, 'Kind/Name', or wikilink.
  AMOUNT: a positive decimal. Required in practice.
  ID: the payment's 8-char id, from `payments list`.
  D, DATE: YYYY-MM-DD.

Flags:
  log:
    -c / --currency  ISO code (default: the thread's)
    -d / --date  date received (default today)
    -t / --time  HH:MM (default now)
    -a / --account  account the money landed in
    -n / --note  free text; takes multiple words
  list: --since and --until (inclusive), --json
  statement:
    --thread  only this thread
    --since, --until  inclusive date range
    --as-of D  statement date; drives aging (default today)
    --pdf PATH  render a PDF to PATH; requires --thread
    --opening D  first day the PDF ledger shows; earlier items collapse into one brought-forward line. Needs --pdf. Cannot be combined with --since or --until, and must not be after --as-of
    --json  JSON output
  show: --json
  edit: --amount, -c / --currency, -d / --date, -t / --time, -a / --account, -n / --note (new values)
  rm: -y / --yes  required to delete

Examples:
  ["log", "Projects/Northwind", "12500.00", "-d", "2026-10-20", "-a", "Business cheque"]
  ["statement", "--thread", "Projects/Northwind", "--json"]
  ["statement", "--thread", "Projects/Northwind", "--pdf", "out/northwind-statement.pdf", "--opening", "2026-07-01"]
  ["rm", "abcd1234", "-y"]

Notes:
  Nothing prompts.
  Records live in threads/<Kind>/<Name>/payments.md, which the tool rewrites. Do not edit that file by hand.
  -n consumes every word that follows it. Put positionals before -n, or put -n last.
  Each `log` queues a REF: in the buffer, filed under the date received. It reaches the thread's daily log on `buffer flush`.
  --pdf needs pandoc and a LaTeX engine, and the thread's client_name frontmatter.
  rm is permanent and fails without -y.
  Exit 1: missing or non-positive amount, --pdf without --thread, --opening without --pdf, --opening with --since or --until, or --opening after --as-of.

BLOCKED: rm. These subcommands are refused and calling one returns an error. Do not attempt them.
